correctness.rationale: Reconstruction: every geodesic of length three connects precisely the missing endpoints and uses one edge from each star plus their indexed interior edge. The unique A,B representation gives rs-ab freely selectable interior edges. A complete maximality case split (A or B empty; both nonempty) yields two exceptional facets and all nonempty pairs with all permissible interior edges. Extremal inequalities and gap follow algebraically. Direct independent shortest-path enumeration agrees coefficientwise through 24 edges; all proof quantifiers are m,n>=3.

value.rationale: This is a motivated metric sensitivity/classification problem: the full biclique has no three-edge geodesics and just one EGP facet, while deleting a single edge creates an exponential family of facets. The exact all-set polynomial and facet polynomial are natural complete invariants over all m,n>=3, and the balanced gap of k-2 facet sizes is a genuine unbounded structural change, not a small numerical increment.
